statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] is the maximum integer L for which there exist indices j_0 < j_1 < ... < j_{L-1} = i such that 0 <= j_0 and obstacles[j_0] <= obstacles[j_1] <= ... <= obstacles[j_{L-1}]. This maximum is the length of the longest nondecreasing obstacle course using only indices at most i and ending at index i.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; in particular, it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or overflow during execution.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = 1 + max({ r[j] | 0 <= j < i and obstacles[j] <= obstacles[i] }), where the maximum of the empty set is defined to be 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 1 <= i < n, if obstacles[i-1] = obstacles[i], then r[i] = r[i-1] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 1 <= i < n, if obstacles[i] < obstacles[i-1], then r[i] <= r[i-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if obstacles[0] <= obstacles[1] <= ... <= obstacles[i], then r[i] = i + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = 1 if and only if for every j with 0 <= j < i, obstacles[j] > obstacles[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r[i] > 1, then there exists an index j such that 0 <= j < i, obstacles[j] <= obstacles[i], and r[i] = r[j] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < n, if obstacles[i] <= obstacles[j], then r[j] >= r[i] + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if obstacles[j] <= obstacles[i] for every j with 0 <= j < i, then r[i] = 1 + max({ r[j] | 0 <= j < i }), where the maximum of the empty set is defined to be 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] <= card({ j | 0 <= j <= i and obstacles[j] <= obstacles[i] }), where card denotes the number of indices in the set.
preconditions: Let n = len(obstacles). 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= obstacles[k] <= 10^7.
